examples.en: A police car is parked in front of my house.
A police car just passed with its siren on.

examples.ko: 사고 현장에 경찰차가 두 대 왔어요.
examples.en: Two police cars came to the scene of the accident.

examples.ko: 우리 아이는 경찰차를 보면 아주 좋아해요.
examples.en: My child loves it when they see a police car.
I drove slowly behind the police car.

examples.ko: 경찰차 소리가 들리면 차들이 길을 비켜 줘요.
examples.en: When cars hear a police car, they make way.

explain: 거리를 돌며 순찰하는 차는 뉴스에서 '순찰차'라고도 자주 불러요. 일상에서는 '경찰차'가 가장 흔해요. '소방차', '구급차'처럼 '차'를 붙여 만든 말이 많아요.
explain_en: A car that patrols the streets is also often called '순찰차' (patrol car) in the news. In daily life '경찰차' is the most common word. Many similar words add '차', like '소방차' (fire truck) and '구급차' (ambulance).

examples.ko: 뒤뜰에서 닭 몇 마리가 모이를 쪼아 먹고 있어요.
examples.en: A few chickens are pecking at feed in the backyard.
There is a persimmon tree in the backyard of Grandma's house.
On the weekend we grilled meat in the backyard.

examples.ko: 뒤뜰 문을 열면 작은 텃밭이 보여요.
examples.en: If you open the back door, you can see a small vegetable garden.
The kids are playing with a ball in the backyard.
The rain stopped, so I hung the laundry in the backyard.

explain: 집 뒤쪽에 있는 뜰이에요. 짝말은 집 앞쪽의 '앞뜰'이고, 일상에서는 '뒷마당'이라고도 말해요. 단독주택이 아니면 쓸 일이 적은 말이에요.
explain_en: It is the yard at the back of a house, and its counterpart is '앞뜰' at the front. In daily talk people also say '뒷마당'. It comes up less if you don't live in a house with a yard.

examples.en: I went to the airport by limousine bus.
The bride and groom got out of a white limousine.

examples.ko: 호텔 앞에 검은 리무진이 서 있었어요.
examples.en: A black limousine was parked in front of the hotel.
The movie star came to the awards ceremony in a limousine.
This limousine is very long.

examples.ko: 공항으로 갈 때는 리무진으로 가면 짐 걱정이 없어요.
examples.en: If you go to the airport by limousine bus, you do not have to worry about luggage.

explain: 한국에서는 긴 고급 승용차뿐 아니라 공항으로 가는 '공항 리무진' 버스도 리무진이라고 불러요. 어느 쪽인지는 앞뒤 말로 알 수 있어요.
explain_en: In Korea, it names not only the long luxury car but also the airport shuttle bus. The surrounding words tell you which one is meant.

examples.en: A horse carriage appears in the old painting.

examples.ko: 마차는 말 두 마리가 끌고 있어요.
examples.en: Two horses are pulling the carriage.
I rode a carriage with the kids in the park.
We loaded the carriage full of luggage.
In the old days people went to the market by carriage.
I was surprised that the carriage's wheels were big.

explain: '마차'는 말이 끄는 것이에요. 소가 끄는 수레는 '소달구지'라고 따로 불러요. 동화나 옛날 이야기, 관광지에서 주로 만날 수 있어요.
explain_en: A '마차' is pulled by horses. A cart pulled by an ox is a separate word, '소달구지'. You mostly meet it in fairy tales, old stories, and tourist spots.

examples.ko: 신문을 배달하려고 매일 숲길을 걸어야 했어요.
examples.en: To deliver newspapers, I had to walk along the forest path every day.
The air felt cool when we entered the persimmon grove path.
Every weekend I take a walk on the forest trail with my family.
It rained earlier, so the forest path is slippery.
There is a small cafe at the end of the forest path.

examples.ko: 이 숲길은 가을에 단풍이 정말 예뻐요.
examples.en: This forest path has really beautiful autumn leaves in the fall.

explain: 산에 난 길은 '산길', 나무가 많은 길은 '숲길'이라고 해요. 보통 '숲길을 걷다', '숲길을 산책하다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: A path on a mountain is a '산길', while a path among many trees is a '숲길'. It is usually used as '숲길을 걷다' or '숲길을 산책하다'.

examples.en: Turn left at the five-way intersection you see over there.
My house is near the five-way intersection.
The five-way intersection is complicated and hard to drive through.
It takes about ten minutes to walk to the five-way intersection.
The traffic light at that five-way intersection is broken.
If you follow this road, you'll reach a five-way intersection.

explain: '삼거리', '사거리'와 짝인 말로, 길이 다섯 갈래로 만나는 곳이에요. 약속 장소나 길 설명에서 기준으로 자주 써요. 지명 이름에 붙기도 해요.
explain_en: It belongs with '삼거리' (three-way junction) and '사거리' (four-way intersection), meaning a place where five roads meet. It is often used as a landmark in directions or meeting spots. It can also be part of place names.

examples.ko: 이 골목은 일방통행이라서 반대로 들어가면 안 돼요.
examples.en: This alley is one-way, so you can't enter from the other side.

examples.ko: 일방통행 표지판을 못 보고 그냥 들어갔어요.
examples.en: I didn't see the one-way sign and just drove in.

examples.ko: 우리 동네 도로가 다음 달부터 일방통행으로 바뀌어요.
examples.en: The road in our neighborhood becomes one-way from next month.
This is a one-way street, but a taxi came the wrong way.

examples.ko: 일방통행 길이라 한참 돌아서 가야 해요.
examples.en: It's a one-way street, so we have to go around for a long way.

examples.ko: 길이 일방통행이 아닌지 먼저 확인해 보세요.
examples.en: First check whether the street is one-way.

explain: 도로 표지판에는 '일방통행'이라고 쓰여 있고, 말로는 '일방통행 길'이라고 해요. 반대로 양쪽으로 다니는 길은 '양방향'이라고 해요. 대화나 관계가 한쪽으로만 흐를 때도 비유로 써요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 한 사람만 말하고 상대의 말은 듣지 않을 때 비판하는 느낌으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used critically when only one person talks and the other's words are not heard.

explain_en: Road signs say '일방통행', and in speech people say '일방통행 길' (a one-way street). A road that goes both ways is '양방향'. It is also used figuratively when a conversation or relationship only goes in one direction.

examples.en: There is a small village on the far side of the river.
Someone over there is waving a hand.
The sun slowly set behind the mountain.
The other side of the road is still under construction.
What kind of country might be across the sea?

examples.ko: 안개가 짙어서 저편이 잘 안 보여요.
examples.en: The fog is thick, so I can't see the far side well.

explain: '이편'과 '저편'은 짝이에요. 말하는 사람에게서 먼 쪽이 저편이고, 가까운 쪽이 이편이에요. 같은 상황에 '저쪽'도 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: '이편' and '저편' are a pair: 저편 is the side far from the speaker and 이편 is the near side. '저쪽' can also be used in the same situation.

examples.en: Grandmother is picking lettuce in the vegetable garden.

examples.ko: 우리 집 뒤에 작은 채소밭이 있어요.
examples.en: There is a small vegetable garden behind our house.
I water the vegetable garden every weekend.
We grow peppers and tomatoes in the vegetable garden.
Lots of weeds have grown in the vegetable garden.

examples.ko: 채소밭은 햇볕이 잘 드는 곳이 좋아요.
examples.en: A vegetable garden should be in a sunny spot.

explain: 집 가까이에 작게 가꾸는 밭은 '텃밭'이라고 많이 해요. '채소밭'은 크기와 상관없이 채소를 기르는 밭이라는 점이 중심이에요. '밭을 갈다', '채소를 키우다'와 자주 함께 써요.
explain_en: A small plot grown near the house is often called a '텃밭'. '채소밭' focuses on the fact that vegetables are grown there, regardless of size. It pairs well with '밭을 갈다' (to plow) and '채소를 키우다' (to grow vegetables).

examples.en: At night the building's entrance door is locked.
This building's entrance door is over there.
Please do not leave luggage in front of the entrance door.

examples.ko: 출입문 옆에 우산을 넣는 통이 있어요.
examples.en: Next to the entrance door there is a bin for umbrellas.
A notice about the day off is posted on the entrance door.

examples.ko: 이 가게 출입문은 자동으로 열리고 닫혀요.
examples.en: This shop's entrance door opens and closes automatically.

explain: 내 집 문은 '현관문', 건물·가게·학교처럼 사람이 많이 드나드는 문은 출입문이라고 구분해요. '출입'은 '나가고 들어오는 것'이라 [추림문]으로 이어서 읽어요.
explain_en: Your own home's door is a '현관문', while the door of a building, shop, or school that many people pass through is a 출입문. It is read connected as [추림문].

examples.en: There are many small cafes along the coast.
If you walk along the coast, the breeze is cool.
The seaside is crowded in summer.
We picked up shells on the seashore.
Many houses on the coast have blue roofs.
The seaside gets quiet too once the sun sets.

explain: '해안'은 바다와 땅이 만나는 곳이고, '-가'를 붙이면 그 근처를 가리켜요. '강가', '길가'도 같은 방식이고 '바닷가'와 거의 같아요.
explain_en: 해안 is where sea meets land, and adding -가 gives the area near it. 강가 and 길가 are formed the same way, and 해안가 is nearly the same as 바닷가.
